content:
According to The Guardian, Apple is in talks with several companies to secure the US broadcasting rights for The Open Championship. Sources indicate that Netflix and Amazon are also expected to show interest in these rights.

The Open Championship began in 1860 in Scotland and is the oldest of the four men's major championships in golf, organised by the R&A. Americans typically refer to it as the "British Open" to distinguish it from the separate major, the US Open.

NBC secured the broadcasting rights for The Open Championship in 2017 with a 12-year contract, outbidding ESPN. The rights are jointly held by Versant, which operates the Golf Channel. The R&A has stated that it expects to hold discussions with NBC and Versant, as well as other parties interested in these rights.

The latest report indicates that Apple has engaged in "preliminary discussions" with the R&A over bidding for The Open Championship. The report cites a "source familiar with the matter," adding that Apple "remains committed to investing in sports broadcasting rights and will continue to seek suitable sports assets."

An R&A spokesperson responded to The Guardian's inquiry as follows:

"Our partnership with NBC and Versant has been excellent, delivering tremendous results for The Open, the AIG Women's Open, as well as our other championships and international events. Looking ahead to the next US media rights cycle for R&A broadcasting rights, we expect to engage with our existing partners NBC and Versant in due course, while continuing to monitor developments in the broadcasting industry and interest in our rights from various parties."

Apple announced last year that it had become the exclusive US broadcasting partner for Formula One. The company also broadcasts Friday Night Baseball and Major League Soccer (MLS) matches.
